# The Guardian Ring

> An educational 3D explainer about infrared satellite architecture, from orbit to a detector element. Public sources explain the physics; named civil instruments supply detailed engineering examples.

Public launch authorized by Reed on 10/05/2026. Pages allow indexing and following. The generated research/gate-results.md records acceptance for its identified build; research/BUILD-REVIEW.md is a historical review. Browser emulation is not physical-device validation.

## Pages

The public site is https://reedos.dev/guardian_ring/.

- [Story](https://reedos.dev/guardian_ring/): The narrated journey, schematic illustrations, engineering paths, and evidence labels.
- [Explorer](https://reedos.dev/guardian_ring/visualizer.html): Light, Data, and Heat views with selectable assemblies, component anatomy, saved comparisons, and independent mathematical examples.
- [Parts](https://reedos.dev/guardian_ring/parts.html): Searchable component names, functions, source-linked explanations, system diagrams, and links into the 3D assemblies.
- [Evidence](https://reedos.dev/guardian_ring/evidence.html): Source register, claim evidence, retained teaching choices, and verification status.
- [Method](https://reedos.dev/guardian_ring/method.html): Formulas, assumptions, and project scope.
- [Glossary](https://reedos.dev/guardian_ring/glossary.html): Physics, spacecraft, optics, electronics, and thermal terminology.

## Explorer and component anatomy

The main journey covers the geosynchronous ring, representative satellite, optical payload, cooled focal-plane package, exploded detector element, and illustrative molecular emission. Side scenes cover the ground segment, civil GOES-R ABI, civil Landsat 9 TIRS-2, and qualitative atmospheric absorption.

The spacecraft exposes structure, solar-wing mechanisms, power regulation and batteries, attitude sensors and actuators, propulsion, command/data handling, communications, and thermal hardware. The payload separates scanning, cover/focus mechanisms, calibration references, optics, detector readout, digitization, command/timing, data interfaces, power, and cooling. The focal-plane view distinguishes a detector array and its ROIC from warm video electronics, bias/timing interfaces, and cold-head temperature feedback.

The Explorer and Parts reference share a canonical component catalog. Its named subcomponents carry source evidence. Three system diagrams explain selected GOES-R support, ABI instrument, and TIRS-2 interface paths, with distinct light, data/control, power, heat, and mechanical connections. These are functional explanations, not complete wiring diagrams.

All 3D geometry is authored in Blender. Spacecraft, payload, and focal-plane story stills use the shipped GLBs. Historical NASA Earth composites are credited and artistically adjusted. Hardware positions, package geometry, wires, fasteners, orbit positions, plume shapes, and drawing colors remain schematic.

## Evidence and scope

Figures are labeled Spec, Vendor, Reported, Calc., or Assumed. Each label leads to the exact source location, formula, or assumption. Sources marked unchecked support no claim. The admitted research ledger currently contains 241 facts from directly inspected public material.

GOES-R, ABI, and TIRS-2 details belong to those named civil designs. TIRS-2's architecture presentation describes a 2018 design. Neither these sources nor the representative drawings describe military sensor internals or performance.

Calculation examples concern orbital geometry, vacuum light travel, ideal circular-aperture diffraction, and ideal blackbody radiation. Source photon radiance is not a detector count, and vacuum propagation time is not warning latency. No real sensor sensitivity, threshold, resolution, array format, false-alarm rate, coverage, or end-to-end performance is estimated.

Atmospheric absorption is qualitative. Molecular emission-band examples come from a civil combustion study. Ground-system sources identify architecture and component roles, not operational algorithms or current operating status. HBTSS and real constellation positions are excluded.

ABI aperture and standalone detector data rate remain unverified. The reviewed sources do not establish analog-amplifier circuitry, ADC precision, standalone ADC packaging, cooler compressor internals, detailed vibration cancellation, connector pinouts, or a specific harness/shielding scheme. Detector material alone does not select an operating temperature. Generic power ratings, battery/recorder capacities, propulsion ratings, real plume intensity, and quantitative atmospheric transmission are not supplied by estimates.

## Publication statement

Personal educational project based on cited public sources. Not an official publication of my employer or of the agencies or companies discussed. Models are schematic; estimates and assumptions are identified.
